Author: S.M.Subramaniam
Bench: S.M.Subramaniam
 W.
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras
 Dated : 10.04.2024
 Coram :
 The Honourable Mr. Justice S.M.Subramaniam
 W.P. No.10020 of 2024
 and
 W.M.P.No.11032, 11033 & 11034 of 2024
 Rev.Fr.R.V.Thomas . 
 Vs.
 1. The District Collector,
 Kanchipuram District,
 Kancheepuram  631 501.
 2. The District Social Welfare Officer,
 District Social Welfare,
 Kancheepuram. 
 3.  The District Differently abled Welfare Officer,
 O/o. The District Differently abled welfare,
 Collectorate Campus,
 Kancheepuram  631 501. ..
 Prayer: Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of I  issuance of writ of Certiorarified Mandamus, to call for the records  to the impugned notice issued by the 2nd r  Na.Ka.No.102/A1/2019 dated 26.03.2024 and quash the same as illegal,
 consequently direct the 2nd respondent not to interfere in the peace  operation of the petitioner's hospice. 
 Page No.1 of 7 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis  W.
 For Petitioner : Mr.R.Prabhakaran Rev.Fr.R.V.Thomas vs The District Collector on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135707283/
1  For R1 to R3 : Mr.N.Naveenkumar  Government Advocate  ORDER The notice issued by the District Social Welfare Officer, Kancheepuram, in Memorandum dated 26.03.2024 is under challenge in the present writ proceedings. 
2. The petitioner states that he is the Managing Trustee of St.Joseph Hospice, for dying destitute established in the year 2011. The petitioner states that the purpose of association is to cater the needs of the people, who all are on the verge of the death. The petitioner states that by collecting donations from the public, he is running the organization and foreign funds are also received by the petitioner. 
3. The memo impugned issued by the 2nd respondent is challenged on the ground that the petitioner is maintaining the House by following the requirements as contemplated under the Senior Citizen Act. The Government https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis is not providing adequate facility to the Senior Citizen, who all are on the verge of the death of their life. Therefore, such private organizations are contributing for the welfare of Senior Citizen. 
4. This court is of the considered opinion that such private organizations registered/recognised are to be maintained in accordance with law. The impugned memorandum dated 26.03.2024 reveals that the District Social Welfare Officer, Kancheepuram asked the petitioner to submit the following documents:
1/fl;ol cWjp rhd;W (Stability Certificate Form A,B,C)
2.Form D Licence (tl;lhl;rpauplkpUe;J bgw ntz;Lk;) 3/Rfhjhur; rhd;W (Sanitary Certificate)
4.jPaizg;g[ rhd;W (Fire Certificate) 5/czt [ ghJfhg;g [ rhd;W (Food Safety Certificate) 
6/Kjpnahu; ,y;y fhg;ghsupd; fhty; JiwaplkpUe;J jilapy;yh rhd;W 7/cs;Siunthu;fs;
kw;Wk; gzpahsu;fspd; tptuk;/ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5. It is the duty of the public Authority to verify the genuinity of the institutions. In the event of any illegality or irregularity, they are empowered to initiate all appropriate actions in the manner known to law. The petitioner is bound to furnish all the requisite documents and comply with the mandatory requirements as contemplated under the Act and Rules. The Authorities Competent are empowered to conduct inspections. 
6. In the present case, the order impugned cannot be construed as a cause for instituting the present writ proceedings and the petitioner is bound to furnish all the Rev.Fr.R.V.Thomas vs The District Collector on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135707283/
2 documents. 
7. Mr.R.Prabhakaran, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner would submit that the documents have already been furnished. 
8. If so, the Authorities Competent are bound to verify the genuinity of the documents, conduct inspections and take a decision by following the procedures as contemplated under the provisions of the Act and Rules in force. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9. Since, the impugned Memorandum has been issued asking the petitioner to submit all the relevant documents and the petitioner states that the documents are already submitted, it is for the respondents to scrutinize the same and conduct inspections by initiating all appropriate actions. If the documents submitted by the petitioner are not in accordance with the Act and Rules, then actions are to be initiated. 
10. With these clarifications, this Writ Petition stands dismissed at the admission stage itself. No costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
